licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets map cleanly onto the dominant clusters visible across all states: fraudulent license procurement, criminal convictions, practice-quality failures (incompetence/negligence), broad unprofessional/ethical conduct, substance abuse impairing practice, mental or physical disability, misleading advertising, violations of statutes/rules/orders (including aiding unlicensed practice, fee-splitting, record falsification, and noncompliance), and adverse actions by other jurisdictions—together covering every item without leaving a meaningful residual.

profession_specific.license_type_structu.rationale: The data splits cleanly by credential type (licensed vs. certified), primary scope (dietitian vs. nutritionist vs. combined), license status (full vs. provisional/temporary), and a small residual group covering technician, associate, compact privilege, and recognized-but-not-issued titles.

profession_specific.alternative_credenti.rationale: The items cluster into named certifications from BCNS (CNS), diplomate credentials from ACBN/ABN, professional society memberships tied to ABN/AIN/ASCN, RD/RDN registration pathways, graduate-degree-based routes, out-of-state license reciprocity, and catch-all board-approved or department-approved credential provisions, together covering every item without a large residual.
